entry.title: Drivers and Risks of Connectivity in Operational Technology Environments
entry.content:
Links: tisiphone.net | lobsters | hacker news

Operational Technology (OT) and Industrial Control Systems (ICS) are integrated into networks to improve efficiency and reduce costs, despite increasing cybersecurity risks. This shift was driven by IT/OT convergence, where bespoke serial-based systems were replaced by standardized Ethernet-based architectures to facilitate easier technical support and logistics.

Connectivity is further driven by the need for real-time telemetry in distributed infrastructure like renewable energy grids and the requirement for remote maintenance by Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs). Implementing security upgrades remains difficult due to the high cost of equipment replacement, the long lifecycles of legacy hardware, and the operational risks associated with modifying critical control systems.

entry.title: Julio Merino Launches ZKeys for Unattended Reboots of Encrypted Disks
entry.content:
Links: jmmv.dev | lobsters

Julio Merino has introduced ZKeys, a managed service designed to enable unattended, passwordless reboots for machines with encrypted disks without compromising data security. The service stores half of an encryption passphrase remotely while the other half remains on the client machine, requiring periodic keepalive pings over HTTPS to keep the volume unlocked.

If a client machine goes offline for an extended period—such as during a physical theft—the server automatically locks access to the key, preventing unauthorized data recovery. The open-source client currently includes integration support for FreeBSD and Fedora, relying on a split-key architecture and encryption at rest to protect against server compromises.

entry.title: Outlook.com Begins Rejecting Emails From Domains Without DMARC Records
entry.content:
Links: mailroute.net | hacker news

Since early November 2026, Microsoft's consumer email services—including Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live, and MSN—have begun rejecting emails from domains that lack a published DMARC record. Unlike previous rules targeting high-volume bulk senders, this enforcement affects low-volume and individual senders, causing intermittent message bounces without public announcements from Microsoft.

Affected domains typically receive a "550 5.7.1 Message rejected" error even if SPF and DKIM are properly configured. Because Microsoft only rejects a portion of mail from non-compliant domains, the issue often goes unnoticed by senders. The problem can be resolved by publishing a basic DMARC TXT record with a policy set to none, provided that SPF or DKIM aligns with the sender's From address.

entry.title: Unconventional IPv4 Addressing and IDNA Mapping Quirks in getaddrinfo
entry.content:
Links: acid.vegas | lobsters | hacker news

An analysis of glibc's getaddrinfo implementation demonstrates how combining the AI_IDN flag with UTS #46 Unicode mapping enables unorthodox characters—including mathematical alphabets, fullwidth digits, circled numbers, and invisible spaces—to translate into valid IPv4 addresses. Because Internationalized Domain Name conversion executes prior to the numeric address parser, various non-standard formats, mixed bases, and lookalike strings successfully resolve to standard IP destinations.

This behavior exposes vulnerabilities in security mechanisms such as SSRF filters, blocklists, and input validators that inspect raw strings instead of resolved endpoints. Attackers can exploit these parsing discrepancies and URL formatting conventions to disguise malicious destinations behind familiar domains or seemingly inert text, highlighting the importance of verifying fully resolved IP addresses rather than raw string inputs.

entry.title: PWN Research Details Firecracker MicroVM Escape and Host Root Execution
entry.content:
Links: pwn.ai | hacker news

PWN Research published a technical write-up detailing a complete escape from an AWS Firecracker microVM (version 1.16.1), demonstrating how a guest can achieve root code execution on the host. By leveraging a previously established host memory access primitive, the technique identifies the Firecracker virtual machine monitor process, maps its virtual memory under ASLR, and locates the active vCPU thread's saved register frame.

The exploit intercepts the return from the KVM ioctl by modifying the saved instruction pointer and stack frame to execute custom host commands before seamlessly resuming normal operation. This compromise preserves guest responsiveness and process stability while highlighting critical security boundaries in container and microVM virtualization setups.

entry.title: SourceHut meta.sr.ht Registration Bypass Vulnerability (CVE-2026-121728)
entry.content:
Links: blog.arusekk.pl | lobsters

A logic error in the SourceHut `meta.sr.ht` platform allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass disabled registration settings. The vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-121728, occurs because the GraphQL backend's `/register/step2` endpoint fails to verify if registration is enabled, even when the frontend indicates that registration is closed. Attackers can bypass the restriction by using a CSRF token obtained from the `/login` endpoint.

The flaw was introduced during an architectural migration from Flask to a Go-based GraphQL backend, where the registration verification was omitted in the new implementation. The vulnerability affects versions 0.56.11 through 0.88.9. A fix has been released following the researcher's disclosure in November 2026.

entry.title: OpenSSH on musl-based Linux Distributions Vulnerable to Password Bypass
entry.content:
Links: sshhole.com | hacker news

OpenSSH installations running on musl libc—including Alpine, OpenWrt, and Buildroot—are vulnerable to a password bypass affecting accounts with no password (marked with '*' in /etc/shadow). When a password longer than 256 characters is provided, musl's crypt() function returns '*' due to a length limit in its SHA512 implementation, which OpenSSH incorrectly validates as a successful match.

The vulnerability specifically affects systems using musl that do not utilize PAM and have password authentication enabled. To mitigate this risk, users are advised to upgrade to OpenSSH 10.6p2 or disable password authentication in their SSH configuration.
